units: bytes and seconds unless named otherwise; no new benchmark or profiling
missing_metrics: No cache hit/miss counters in any of the 48 response stats.
No prefill expert-demand bytes, SSD-read duration, physical disk bytes, or critical-vs-masked I/O split.
No per-phase process-compression/decompression or memory snapshots. Memory is sampled at ready and after each complete generation.
No exclusive CPU/GPU/synchronization/idle attribution, kernel timings, factory-cache hit/eviction counters, allocation count, thermal frequency or command-buffer occupancy in these reports.
Report environment filters MLXL3_*; MLX_MAX_OPS_PER_BUFFER and MLX_MAX_MB_PER_BUFFER require frozen plan/identity evidence.

interpretation.claim: The measured DF HOLD prefill slowdown repeats in both ON processes and is absent on their warmup HOLD responses.
interpretation.scope: Only two measured responses per arm, fixed four-response order, no crossover of prompt order.

interpretation.claim: DF measured HOLD logical decode expert-demand bytes, speculative widths/rows and proposed/accepted/block counts are identical in all arms. No profile evidence of increased logical decode reads.
Measured DF HOLD verification time is slightly lower on average for ON, and draft/commit timings remain close. These decode-only clocks cannot explain or measure the prefill penalty.

DF ON measured HOLD has more process decompressions since the previous completion report (50577 and39355) than OFF (28709 and27445). Sampling spans inter-request work plus complete prefill and decode, so the extra decompressions cannot be assigned to prefill.
DF ON process3 also has47746 additional process decompressions before its measured MAIN completion while that MAIN prefill remains normal. Decompression count alone does not isolate the slow prefill.
No large ON-specific active-memory or footprint increase accompanies the slow HOLD; native process-ledger swapin values are zero and external inspections report zero cumulative new Swapout.

No causal attribution to I/O, JIT/cache-factory churn, memory donation/copying, precise exp, compression stalls or GPU/CPU idle is possible from these response aggregates. A source defect or targeted preregistered diagnostic is needed before correction.

memory_delta_scope: Differences between ready/previous completion and current completion, including any inter-request reset/configuration/cleanup; not exclusive perfill/decode samples. process_decompressions counts pages per API, not disk reads or time.
io_scope: dflash_profile.expert_demand_bytes is a logical decode demand counter; it is not physical SSD traffic or critical-path time.
